title: Choosing Where to Park: Candidate Places Round the Target, a Score That Trades Reach Margin Against Travel and Clearance, and Saying None

questions.question: Why is the margin in the ring part of the score?
options: It is the distance the base has to drive
It is the clearance from the nearest obstacle
It is the room the base has to stop short or long and still reach
It is how far the arm is from a singularity
questions.explanation: A base that parks in the middle of the ring can miss by the whole tolerance. One that parks at the edge reaches only if it stops exactly.

questions.question: With travel weighted most the base travelled:
options: 0 m: it reached from where it stood
questions.explanation: It stopped at the near edge of the ring after 1.24 m. With no weight on travel it went 2.56 m to the place with the most margin.

questions.question: With obstacles all round the target, how many places were free?
options: 252, all of them
36, one distance all the way round
7, one bearing
questions.explanation: Every one of the 252 candidates put the base within its radius and the clearance of some obstacle, so the answer was none.

questions.question: Where did the base go when a row of obstacles blocked the near side?
options: To the near edge of the ring, between two obstacles
To a bearing of -170 degrees, as with nothing in the way
Nowhere: it said none
Round to a bearing of -30 degrees
questions.explanation: The candidates on the blocked side were rejected before scoring, and the best of the rest was on the far side.

questions.question: What do the weights decide?
options: How many candidates are tried
Whether to arrive soon, with room, or clear of things
Which candidates are rejected for obstacles
How wide the ring is
questions.explanation: Margin, travel and clearance pull different ways, and no place is best at all three. The weights are where that choice is written down.

questions.question: What must a choice be able to say?
options: The nearest place, even if it is not free
None
The best of the rejected places
The place it chose the last time
questions.explanation: When no candidate is free the caller has to hear that, and then ask for less margin, another approach, or stop.
